The Three Domain System
¨Domain Archaea
¤Prokaryotic unicellular organisms that reproduce asexually.
¤Live in extreme environments.
¤Cell wall is diverse but not the same as the bacterial cell wall.
¨Domain Eukarya
¤Unicellular and multicellular organisms
¤Cells with a membrane-bounded nucleus
¤Sexual reproduction is common
¤Contains four kingdoms
  nKingdom Protista
  nKingdom Fungi
  nKingdom Plantae
  nKingdom Animalia
explanation: This slide contrasts Domain Archaea and Domain Eukarya. Domain Archaea consists of prokaryotic, unicellular organisms that reproduce asexually and typically live in extreme environments. Their cell walls are chemically diverse but distinct from those of bacteria. Domain Eukarya encompasses both unicellular and multicellular organisms whose cells contain a membrane-bounded nucleus. In this domain, sexual reproduction is common. Domain Eukarya is divided into four kingdoms: Kingdom Protista, Kingdom Fungi, Kingdom Plantae, and Kingdom Animalia.

questions.q: Which domain contains prokaryotic organisms that are known for living in extreme environments and have cell walls different from bacteria?
questions.exp: Domain Archaea consists of prokaryotes that live in extreme environments and have cell walls chemically distinct from Domain Bacteria.

questions.q: What are the four kingdoms contained within Domain Eukarya?
questions.exp: Domain Eukarya contains four kingdoms: Kingdom Protista, Kingdom Fungi, Kingdom Plantae, and Kingdom Animalia.
